correctness.rationale: The proof explicitly defines normalized Hodge error and all domains. It cites the published all-graph deterministic energy identity, derives five exact joint edge/wedge moments and verifies them by 40 rational checks and 74 separate direct game projections. The first-edge Poisson limit uses vanishing expected wedges, the sparse law uses L2 convergence, and the Gaussian law uses a connected-overlap cumulant argument yielding the exact bivariate covariance matrix and delta-method variance. Dense behavior follows from exact relative-variance bounds. Zero-edge and centering boundaries are explicit. Numerical tests do not stand in for the infinite proof.

The inspected primary paper, relevant probability references and semantic claim searches do not give the particular Erdős–Rényi two-threshold game-error classification, the Bernoulli first-contact law, or the sharp joint edge–wedge Gaussian coefficient. This is a best-knowledge comparison, not proof of absolute publication priority; the finite-graph formula is explicitly attributed.

value.rationale: The graphwise deterministic potential-surrogate error becomes a policy-relevant random quantity when conflict topology is uncertain. The theorem determines the two natural structural thresholds at which any conflicts appear and adjacent conflicts become common, then quantifies the full Gaussian finite-size risk at fixed expected degree. The three laws and sharp coefficient give nontrivial, naturally motivated stochastic benchmarks beyond the deterministic graph identity, without claiming safety or welfare effects outside its normalization.
